transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because the thought of seeing a rat has just gotten so bad that I can’t do parts of my job anymore. I'm a building cleaner, and... I mean, I know it’s probably just an old building or a trash room, and it's not really dangerous, but the fear is just stopping me from working.
When you see a rat—or even think you might encounter one, like in a trash room—what happens to you in that moment? Can you describe the fear you feel?

It happens right away. If I just hear a scratching sound near a wall, or see something move by a pipe, my whole body reacts. My heart starts pounding, my hands start shaking... and I just feel like I have to get out of there before I can even think straight.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear reaction to rats or the possibility of encountering them?

It's been about two years now. It started right around the time I moved into this older apartment building. People there just kept talking about rats being around, and... well, ever since then, it's been like this.
Aside from rats, do you experience this same intense fear with other animals or in other situations, or is it specifically tied to rats?
No, it's really just the rats. I mean, I don't have a problem with spiders or dogs or... anything else, really. I'm fine with all that. It's specifically just rats that make me panic like this.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms fear is isolated exclusively to rats, with no other animal or situational fears, supporting a specific phobia diagnosis limited to this trigger. Two-year duration and functional impairment (unable to perform job duties) further support the diagnosis.
